title: Light in flat space
demoNote: The moving ray and the u curve come from your own equation, solved with RK4 in the browser, and checked against the exact answer u = sin(φ) ÷ b.

beats.text: Before we bend any light, let's watch it travel straight, with no black hole at all.
This ray passes a centre point. The closest it ever gets is a distance called b, the impact parameter.
As the light moves, we track r, its distance from the centre, and phi, the angle it has swept around.
Instead of r, we use u, which is one divided by r. Far away, r is huge, so u is almost zero.
beats.speech: Instead of r, we use u, which is one divided by r. Far away, r is huge, so u is almost zero.

beats.text: In flat space, u follows one simple rule: u equals the sine of phi, divided by b.
Watch the graph. u starts at zero, rises to its peak at the closest point, and falls back to zero when phi reaches pi.
That return to zero at phi equals pi is exactly your Stage 1 check. In Stage 2, one extra term will bend this line.

explore.prompt: Drag b. Watch the ray and the peak of the u curve.

tasks.prompt: If b doubles, what happens to the peak of u?
hints: Drag b from 5 to 10 and watch the top of the curve.
The peak is where sine phi equals one. So the peak is one divided by b.

why.double: Not quite. A bigger b means the ray passes further away, so r is bigger and u, one over r, gets smaller.
why.same: Not quite. The peak is one divided by b, so it depends on b. Try dragging b and watch the top of the curve.

tasks.explain: Right. The peak is one divided by b. Double b and the ray passes twice as far away, so u at its peak is half as big.

tasks.prompt: At what angle φ does the ray leave again, with u back to 0?
hints: Look at the graph. Where does the curve touch zero again?
Sine is zero at phi equals zero, and at one more angle before two pi.
tasks.tooLow: Not yet. At that angle the ray is still passing by, so u is not back to zero. Look further along the graph.
tasks.tooHigh: Too far. The ray has already left before that angle. Look where the curve first touches zero again.
tasks.explain: Right. The ray leaves at phi equals pi. Your RK4 run lands there too. That is the Stage 1 check.

recap: So: b is the closest approach. u is one over r. And in flat space, u equals sine phi over b, returning to zero at phi equals pi.
